d: The American midterms have reopened an argument older than the United States itself: how does a democracy protect its liberties from the personal ambitions of those elected to govern it? The question belongs to every democracy, even if the consequences of America’s experience travel unusually far and wide. Americans have repudiated the Trump administration's performance, but not necessarily Trumpism itself. An election cannot, by itself, repair institutions or reverse years of political mistrust.
